about: Fees and decision times for the work permit routes in work.json, and for visitor visas by destination,, researched on November 14, 2026 (the owner's command of that day: research, then estimate). Each entry names its source and whether it is the government's own page (official) or another publication (secondary). days is calendar days, or [shortest, longest] where the source gives a range; stayDays is how long the permission lasts at most, where the source says.

US.route: O-1 (extraordinary ability in the arts, or extraordinary achievement in motion pictures or television)
US.feeBasis: Form I-129 for an O petition filed on paper, $1,055, and the Asylum Program Fee a regular petitioner pays, $600.
US.daysBasis: Standard processing of an O-1 petition, three to six months in 2026.
US.stayBasis: An O-1 is granted for up to three years.

sources.what: USCIS Form G-1055 Fee Schedule, edition 10/26/26, Appendix A: I-129 O petition and Asylum Program Fee
Standard I-129 processing, 3 to 6 months for O-1 petitions (July 2026)

GB.feeBasis: The application fee for each person applying, the same inside or outside the UK.
GB.daysBasis: A decision usually within 3 weeks when applying from outside the UK.
GB.stayBasis: Up to 12 months, or the certificate of sponsorship's time plus up to 28 days, whichever is shorter.

sources.what: GOV.UK, Creative Worker visa (Temporary Work): how much it costs, how long it takes

CA.daysBasis: Two to five months from outside Canada, depending on where the application is made.

sources.what: IRCC fee list: Work permit (including extensions) – per person, $155.00
Processing time, 2 to 5 months

AU.route: Temporary Activity visa (subclass 408), Entertainment Activities stream
AU.feeBasis: The base application charge for the main applicant from July 1, 2026.
AU.daysBasis: Half of applications decided in 23 days and nine in ten in 47, from the department's published times (September 2026).

sources.what: Visa application charges: subclass 408 Entertainment Activities stream, AUD535
Processing times for the 408 Entertainment Activities stream, from Home Affairs (September 2026)

NZ.feeBasis: The cost from NZD 1,355, by where the applicant applies from.

sources.what: Immigration New Zealand, Entertainers Work Visa: cost and processing time

IE.route: Atypical Working Scheme permission (beyond 90 days, an Employment Permit)
IE.feeBasis: The non-refundable processing fee, paid when the application is submitted.
IE.daysBasis: A minimum of 20 working days: four calendar weeks.
IE.stayBasis: The scheme covers work of up to 90 days.

sources.what: Irish Immigration Service, Atypical Working Scheme: fee and processing times

FR.route: Carte de séjour « talent – profession artistique et culturelle »
FR.feeBasis: The long-stay visa (type D) marked « passeport talent – profession artistique et culturelle », issued by the consulate.

sources.what: Artiste étranger, carte talent: procédure (updated June 2026)

DE.route: Aufenthaltserlaubnis zur Beschäftigung (Kultur und Unterhaltung, § 25 BeschV)
DE.feeBasis: The fee for a national visa (category D) for employment, § 45 (2) of the Residence Ordinance.
DE.daysBasis: About four weeks as a German mission states it, longer where the Federal Employment Agency must approve.

sources.what: German Consulate General Hong Kong, national visa for employment: the €75 fee
Work visa: €75 for a national visa for employment (§ 45 (2) AufenthV); processing times
